info.title: ProxyShop merchant service
info.description: Code minting, Shopify webhooks, the pixel collector, and envelope administration. The envelope routes are SEALED state (C3/S7): the exchange has no grant to read them and `.importlinter` forbids the import.

get.summary: Begin an install: redirect the merchant to Shopify's authorize screen.
get.description: Served and declared nowhere until T-317. It is a browser redirect rather than a cross-domain service call, which is exactly why it was left out — and exactly why it was never reviewed. It is unauthenticated, it takes a caller-supplied `shop`, and it issues a signed install state; a surface with those three properties belongs in the contract.

302.description: Redirect to Shopify's OAuth authorize screen, carrying the signed install state.

400.description: `shop` is not a shop domain this app will talk to.

503.description: No Shopify API key/secret is configured, so no state can be issued or verified.

get.summary: Verify Shopify's redirect, exchange the code, store the offline token, install.
get.description: The other half of the OAuth pair, and the more sensitive one: it consumes the install state, spends an authorization code and stores an offline token. A forged, tampered and expired state all answer the same 400 on purpose — telling them apart is a signal handed to whoever is guessing.

200.description: The install that was completed: scopes granted, pixel installed, webhooks registered.

400.description: The state is unknown, or the shop it was issued for is not the shop that came back.

401.description: The callback's own HMAC did not verify.

502.description: Shopify was unreachable or refused the exchange. Not this app being broken.

503.description: No Shopify API key/secret is configured.

get.summary: Every shop this process holds an offline token for. Administrative; bearer-guarded.
get.description: An administrative JSON endpoint, not a browser redirect — the reason T-317 refused the 'it is only the OAuth pair' exemption. It enumerates every installed merchant, and it refuses every caller until MERCHANT_ADMIN_TOKEN is configured.

200.description: The shops with a stored offline token.

401.description: No bearer token, or one that does not match.

503.description: No administrative token is configured, so the route refuses everyone.

post.summary: Mint a single-use discount code and cart permalink for a winning offer.
post.description: Creates a discountCodeBasicCreate with usageLimit 1 and an expiry no further out than 48h, and validates combinesWith before returning.

201.description: The code and the permalink the buyer follows.

post.summary: Receive a Shopify webhook and record it as a LedgerEvent.
post.description: The authoritative record for reconciliation (R4). `orders/paid` becomes an `order_paid` LedgerEvent joined to the pixel observation on `checkout_token` (D24).

post.summary: Receive one client-side checkout observation from the Web Pixel.
post.description: Lossy and never authoritative (R4). It is joined to the webhook on `checkout_token`; the pixel spells its client id `clientId`, which is why `contracts.join_key_view()` is the only reader of these keys.

get.description: Administrative. Requires the merchant admin bearer token; an unconfigured deployment refuses every caller with 503 rather than serving sealed state anonymously.

put.summary: Replace a store's envelope, creating a new version.
put.description: Administrative, and NOT self-activating. The body is the merchant's *request*: `version` is ignored (it is derived from what is already on file) and `activation: "active"` is honoured only when the request also carries an `X-Envelope-Approval` artifact bound to the terms being stored. Without one the new version is written in `shadow` — the edit is not lost — and the call answers 403 `approval-required` naming the missing paperwork (R6/E5).

parameters.name: X-Envelope-Approval
parameters.description: The merchant's recorded written approval of these exact terms, as a JSON object. `envelope_hash` is what binds it: a SHA-256 over the canonical rendering of the seven approved-terms fields plus `version`, so an approval lifted off a different envelope authorizes nothing. `approved_at` must carry a timezone. `note` and `document_ref` are optional; any other key is refused. Required only to move an envelope to `active`; a `shadow` write needs none.

200.description: The stored envelope. `activation` is `active` only when a bound approval accompanied the request.

400.description: The body is not a readable envelope, or `X-Envelope-Approval` is present and is not a JSON object.

example.detail: X-Envelope-Approval must carry a JSON object, got list

401.description: No bearer token, or the wrong one.

403.description: The body asked for `activation: "active"` and no approval artifact bound to these terms accompanied it. The new version IS on file, in `shadow`; nothing was activated.

example.detail: no written approval artifact was recorded; an envelope is never activated on anybody's say-so alone (R6)

409.description: The body names another store, or a version already superseded.

get.summary: R9's whole merchant page for one store, in one read.
get.description: Everything R9 names, assembled server-side: the versioned envelope and the bidding decision derived from it, the exchange's win/loss report aggregated by intent cluster with reason categories only, this store's trust snapshot with its per-dimension breakdown, the trust event payloads behind it, and the log of solicitations this dashboard has made against the store's own agent. NO RIVAL AMOUNTS AND NO RIVAL IDENTITIES: the loss report's suppression is the exchange's own projection, and the trust snapshot is narrowed to the calling store HERE, on the server, because `GET /snapshot` answers every store at once and narrowing in a browser means the rival's rows were already served to it. The exchange's report bearer is held by this service and never reaches the browser: at the exchange that token IS the store's identity.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Loss window start, epoch seconds. Defaults to 30 days ago, echoed back.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Loss window end, epoch seconds. Defaults to now, echoed back.

200.description: The page. Every region is a panel carrying its own state.

envelope.description: One region of the page. `state` is `ok`, `absent`, `not_configured` (with `missing` naming the environment variables to set), `unauthorized`, `unreachable` or `upstream_refused`. Rows are present ONLY in `ok`: a refusal never renders as an empty result, because an empty loss list reads as 'you lost nothing'.

post.summary: Ask this store's own agent for a bid, and record what it answered.
post.description: This is how R9's kill switch becomes OBSERVABLE. The merchant service posts a real `BidRequest` to the store agent's published `POST /v1/bid-requests` - the same door the exchange solicits through - and records the answer verbatim: a `Bid`, or the contract's 204 decline whose reason travels in `x-proxyshop-decline-reason` (`store_killed`, `envelope_not_activated`, ...). Kill the store, solicit again, and the row that comes back is the proof. It is a REHEARSAL and every row says so (`origin: dashboard`); it is not the live auction log, whose per-auction rationale lives in the agent's own in-process shadow log and has no served route. The body is optional: anything omitted is defaulted from the store's own envelope, the cluster from `pursue_clusters`, so a rehearsal is not answered `cluster_not_pursued` for a cluster the merchant never asked to pursue. The pseudonym is a fixed synthetic value and never a buyer's (R5).

example.query: a warm mid-layer for cold commutes

contradiction.description: The merchant stopped this store and its agent bid anyway. Reachable today: the merchant service holds the authoritative envelope and nothing delivers it to a separately deployed agent, which reads its own STORE_AGENT_CONTEXT once at start-up.
